maria_support: FYI — customer BrightFrame reports large drop in vectors/sec after a midnight config roll. Tokens/sec looks steady but vectors/sec ~50-70% lower than baseline. No 5xx, just slow responses. Request sample id: bf-req-9a7c
jamal_oncall: Are they using our embeddings endpoint or a variant? Any recent model/quantization swap?
ingrid_research: They reported model=redwood-embed-1536-v2 and batch_size hinted at 64 in client logs. Maria, can you paste a sample request header?
maria_support: header pasted: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***`, `X-Model-ID: redwood-embed-1536-v2`, `Content-Type: application/json` and body shows array length 64 of strings. No client-side retries.
ryan_ops: Ok. Quick checks I ran: nvtop snapshot show one GPU at 95% util but kernel wait increases and GPU queue depth for our infer runtime jumped vs last week: queue_depth 54 -> 210 during peak. Memory ok.
sre_bot: deploy-bot: rolled redwood-serving/rt -> v2.14.3 @ 2024-11-08T00:12:35Z (canary->prod).
jamal_oncall: That rollout could've changed batching heuristics. If tokens/sec is same but vectors/sec drops, maybe per-request pre/post processing added overhead or batch alignment changed so smaller effective batch per-vector.
ingrid_research: Another angle: kv-cache/prefix caching might be disabled for emb model variants in that build (we had a config flip to avoid KV serialization races). Without prefix caching we do more CPU prep per item which can reduce vectors/sec. Maria, any logs showing kvcache hits/misses?
maria_support: customer logs don't surface kvcache. I pulled server logs (excerpt):
```
2024-11-08T00:45:12Z INFO embed_request id=bf-req-9a7c batch_count=4 total_inputs=64 effective_batch_sizes=[16,16,16,16] kvcache_hits=0 kvcache_misses=64 queue_wait_ms=82 gpu_wait_ms=210
```
ryan_ops: That is interesting — effective_batch_sizes=16 despite client sending 64. Means our splitter/autosplit is chopping into many small sub-batches. That could explain queue thrash.
jamal_oncall: Possible causes: a) per-request tokenization variance causing uneven packing b) a bug in batching window calculation after the rollout c) routing to a different kernel variant that has stricter sequence-length bucketing.
ingrid_research: Quick repro steps for support to validate: 1) run curl against /v1/embeddings with 1) 64 identical short strings, 2) 64 long strings to change sequence length distribution. Compare `X-Req-Id` and check server logs for `effective_batch_sizes` and `kvcache_hits`. Example curl:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Model-ID: redwood-embed-1536-v2" \
  -d '{"input": ["short","short",... 64x ]}' -o /tmp/short.json
```
Also collect `tokens_per_sec` and `vectors_per_sec` scores from /internal/metrics?req=$X_REQ_ID.
maria_support: I'll run the short/long repro against their account and share log snippets. Also asked them to try `batch_size=32` to see if larger fragmentation stops.
ryan_ops: Until root cause we can mitigate by: - pinning routing to older runtime `v2.14.2` for that customer - temporarily forcing client-level `batch_size=32` or less - enabling a config to prefer packing by embeddings count instead of token budget (I can flip per-cust flag)
jamal_oncall: Good. Maria, please collect reproducible curl output + server log lines (embed_request entries) and also the customer's observed latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99). Tag me and @ingrid when you have them. :thumbsup:
maria_support: Will do. Pushing repro now and will paste logs here when done.
sre_bot: metric-alert: embeddings.vecs_throughput_drop customer=BrightFrame severity=warning current=46% baseline=100% triggered at 2024-11-08T01:10:02Z
